s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of painful lower-extremity nodules and polyarthralgia with systemic inflammation
salient_findings: Painful nodules on the anterior shins and inner left thigh
Edematous and tender left wrist, hand, and metacarpophalangeal joints with marked synovitis
Extensive edema and varicosities in bilateral lower extremities
key_facts: 71-year-old man
Recurrent bladder cancer post-resection and local chemotherapy
Coronary artery disease
Essential hypertension with diastolic dysfunction
Tobacco use
Painful lower-extremity nodules and polyarthralgia developing over several months
Serum lipase >20,000 U/L
Amylase 7,914 U/L
Extensive autoimmune and infectious work-up negative
Cancer markers: CA 19-9: 118 U/L, CEA: 2.6 ng/mL
Multiple cystic lesions within pancreatic head on CT and MRCP
1.9 × 1.7-cm mass in portal vein with extension to superior mesenteric vein on EUS
Cutaneous lesion biopsy showing 'Ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification
Synovial fluid aspirate with no crystals, leukocytes, or bacteria on gram stain

shortlist.label: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum lipase and amylase, multiple cystic lesions within pancreatic head, and mass in portal vein with extension to superior mesenteric vein

shortlist.label: Pancreatic metastasis from bladder cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of recurrent bladder cancer and presence of multiple cystic lesions within pancreatic head

shortlist.label: Chronic pancreatitis with pseudocyst
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum lipase and amylase, and presence of multiple cystic lesions within pancreatic head

shortlist.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
shortlist.why_kept: Negative autoimmune and infectious work-up, and presence of systemic inflammation

shortlist.label: Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum lipase and amylase, and presence of cutaneous lesion biopsy showing 'Ghost cells'—fat necrosis with saponification

raw.rationale: The patient's elevated serum lipase and amylase levels, multiple cystic lesions within the pancreatic head, and a mass in the portal vein with extension to the superior mesenteric vein are highly suggestive of pancreatic adenocarcinoma. The presence of 'ghost cells' indicating fat necrosis with saponification in the cutaneous lesion biopsy also supports this diagnosis, as it is a known complication of pancreatic adenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Pancreatic metastasis from bladder cancer
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of bladder cancer, the presence of a primary mass in the pancreas and the specific imaging and laboratory findings point more towards a primary pancreatic malignancy rather than a metastasis.

rejected.label: Chronic pancreatitis with pseudocyst
rejected.why: The acute presentation and the specific findings of a mass in the portal vein and multiple cystic lesions within the pancreatic head are not typical for chronic pancreatitis with pseudocyst.

rejected.label: Autoimmune pancreatitis
rejected.why: The extensive autoimmune and infectious work-up was negative, and the presence of a distinct mass and cystic lesions in the pancreas does not align with the typical presentation of autoimmune pancreatitis.

rejected.label: Pancreatic acinar cell carcinoma
rejected.why: While this is a possible diagnosis, the combination of the patient's clinical presentation, laboratory findings, and imaging results more strongly supports pancreatic adenocarcinoma, which is more common and has a broader range of presentations that can include the findings described.
